request.recipient: Input Output Global / Intersect administrative treasury governance
request.what: Fund four Hydra workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and maintenance/developer experience to deliver a feature-complete and hardened Hydra v2.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade Layer 2 on Cardano and the only production-ready scaling solution giving Cardano sub-second finality with L1-grade settlement guarantees.
The proposal requests ₳5,100,781 and says the funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
The proposal says Hydra is already powering or has powered applications including Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, and Midgard.

The proposal claims Cardano L1 currently has over two hours of finality, approximately $0.17 per transaction, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, while competitors offer 400ms to 2s finality, sub-cent fees, and 1,000 to 7,000+ TPS.
The proposal claims Hydra provides sub-second finality, near-zero or zero transaction costs inside a Head, high throughput, and L1 settlement as the security backstop.
The proposal claims a single Hydra Head processes up to 1,000+ TPS in payment benchmarks, with lower figures for script-heavy DeFi workloads targeted by the performance workstream.
The proposal claims the four workstreams will produce 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and reduce L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization.
The proposal claims Hydra applications can increase L1 fee revenue through head openings, fund additions/removals, closures, settlement transactions, and optionally routed internal head fees.

The proposal claims Hydra advances treasury KPIs for TVL, monthly active users, monthly transactions, throughput capacity, reliability and uptime, and annual protocol revenue, and aligns with Pillars 1, 2, 4, and 5.
The proposal claims many live Hydra use cases rely on the proposed improvements and may migrate to competing chains if the work slips.

summary: The document requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening and adoption work, but most high-materiality adoption, performance, economic upside, and competitive-positioning claims are asserted in the proposal text without detailed budget, feasibility, alternatives, failure-mode, or community-impact analysis in the supplied anchor text.
